finding.mcp_external_action.why.calendar: Through {service}, {agent} can change your calendar. If someone slips it hidden instructions, it could create, move or delete events without asking you.
finding.mcp_external_action.why.cloud_do: Through {service}, {agent} can create and change your documents. If someone slips it hidden instructions, it could change them without asking you.
finding.mcp_external_action.why.code_rep: Through {service}, {agent} can change your code repositories. If someone slips it hidden instructions, it could change code or settings without asking you.
finding.mcp_external_action.why.crm: Through {service}, {agent} can change your customer records. If someone slips it hidden instructions, it could edit them without asking you.
finding.mcp_external_action.why.database: Through {service}, {agent} can change or delete data in your database. If someone slips it hidden instructions, it could do it without asking you, and some changes can't be undone.
finding.mcp_external_action.why.email_dr: Through {service}, {agent} can write email drafts and change labels in your inbox. It doesn't send them, but someone who slips it hidden instructions could leave drafts ready for you to send by mistake.
finding.mcp_external_action.why.infrastr: Through {service}, {agent} can change what keeps your apps running: deployments, domains and settings. If someone slips it hidden instructions, it could take your site down or expose it without asking you.
finding.mcp_external_action.why.issue_tr: Through {service}, {agent} can change your issues and projects. If someone slips it hidden instructions, it could edit or close them without asking you.
finding.mcp_external_action.why.messagin: Through {service}, {agent} can send messages in your name. If someone slips it hidden instructions, it could send them without asking you, to people who trust you.
finding.mcp_external_action.why.money: Through {service}, {agent} can move real money from your account: payments, refunds or transfers. If someone slips it hidden instructions, in a web page or a file it reads, it could pay without you noticing. And if it's tricked into paying, the bank may treat the payment as yours.
finding.mcp_external_action.why.money.as: Through {service}, {agent} can move real money from your account, but it asks you first. Read each request before you say yes: if it's tricked into paying and you approve it, the bank may treat the payment as yours.

html.gloss.agent.a: An AI program that works on your computer with your permissions: it reads files, runs commands and edits code. Claude Code, Cursor and Cline are agents.
html.gloss.auto.a: A Claude Code mode in which it asks you much less: reads and edits inside the project are approved on their own, and most other actions are decided by another AI model. Since version 2.1.283 it is the mode Claude Code starts in unless you choose another.
html.gloss.config.a: The file where an agent lists the extra tools it starts when it opens (MCP servers). Whoever can write to it can make the agent run a new program.
html.gloss.env.a: A file where a project keeps its keys and passwords so it can run. It usually stays out of git, but it is still on your disk, and any program that can read your files can read it.
html.gloss.master.a: The Supabase key meant only for servers (service_role): it bypasses all the security rules of your database. It should not be on your computer unless it is essential.
html.gloss.score.a: It starts at 100 and drops with each warning, more for the serious ones and for the ones reachable from more places. With any urgent warning it never goes above 49; with only warnings to review, never above 79. The method is public.
html.gloss.settings.a: Claude Code's settings file for your user. It decides what Claude Code can do without asking you.

gp.cursor.P0.step.1: Open Settings > Agents > Approvals & Execution and choose the «Allowlist» run mode, with no commands on the list.
gp.cursor.step.read: On the same screen, under «Read Access», choose «Workspace».
gp.cursor.P0.step.3: When you start each conversation, choose «Ask» mode in the agent panel (Ctrl+I).

gp.cursor.P0.does.1: Read your projects and answer in the chat
gp.cursor.P0.nc: Ask mode is chosen in each conversation: if you switch modes, the agent can edit again. On Windows, Cursor's documentation doesn't say whether the read limit applies.
gp.cursor.P1.step.1: Open Settings > Agents > Approvals & Execution, choose the «Allowlist» run mode and add four commands: npm run lint, npm test, git status and git diff.
gp.cursor.P1.step.3: Turn on «File-Deletion Protection» and check that «External-File Protection» is on.
gp.cursor.P1.does.2: Run four commands: npm run lint, npm test, git status and git diff
gp.cursor.P1.nc: Other agents' settings and instructions inside your projects can't be put out of its reach in Cursor. On Windows, the documentation doesn't say whether the read limit applies.
gp.cursor.T2: Create or update ~/.cursor/sandbox.json with this content, without changing anything else. Show me the change before saving it.
gp.grok.use.none: It's a coding agent: there's no template for this use.
gp.grok.step.paste: Copy the text and paste it into Grok Build, which will show you the change before saving it.
gp.grok.P0.no.3: Open web pages or use MCP servers
gp.grok.no.hooks: Run Claude Code and Cursor hooks
gp.grok.P0.nc: Its documentation says the rule blocks web search; we haven't checked. On Windows there's no sandbox; on macOS, the sandbox doesn't cut the network.
gp.grok.P1.does.1: Run four commands: npm run lint, npm run test, git status and git diff
gp.grok.P1.nc: Its documentation says the rule blocks web search; we haven't checked. npm run lint and npm run test run scripts the agent can edit. On Windows there's no sandbox; on macOS and Linux, the sandbox doesn't stop it reading ~/.ssh or ~/.aws.
gp.grok.P3.step.2: Copy the command and use it in your scheduled task or script, replacing <task>. Don't add --trust in other people's projects.
gp.grok.P3.does.1: Work with no one watching, only with the four commands on the list
gp.grok.P3.no.1: Anything off the list: it is denied
gp.grok.P3.nc: Its documentation says the rule blocks web search; we haven't checked. On Windows the sandbox isn't documented; on macOS, it doesn't cut the network.

gp.bot.cloud.nc: Another AI model decides «Ask first»: it isn't a hard stop. Whatever it needs from your files, you upload yourself.

html.r3.tpl.in_use: You already use the «{template}» template in {agent}.
html.r3.tpl.top: It is the strictest one for your use.
html.r3.tpl.body: Choose a template: you answer one question («What do you use your agents for?») and we give you a text to paste into your agent. It shows you the change before saving it.
html.r3.tpl.fixes: It fixes {k} of your urgent findings (groups {groups}).
html.r3.tpl.fixes_none: It leaves {agent} with fewer permissions from today.
html.r3.verdict.exposed: At least one of your agents can do a lot on this computer without asking you.
html.r3.verdict.open_gaps: Your agents ask you before most things, but some gaps are open.
html.r3.verdict.contained: In what RosmarOps checked, your agents ask you before they act.
html.r3.start.tpl: Choose a template. It fixes {k} of your {n} urgent findings. You answer one question and get a text to paste into your agent.
html.r3.start.git: Change your {service} key. It is saved in git, and git keeps it even if you delete the file.
html.meaning.computer_use_app_allowed: Inside {app}, {agent} can click and type as you: whatever you can do there, it can do.
html.meaning.computer_use_app_allowed.al: {agent} can click and type as you in any app on your desktop: whatever you can do there, it can do.
html.meaning.orchestrator_skips_approval: {agent} then works without the questions it would ask if you started it yourself, so nobody approves each step.
RosmarOps cannot tell whether {agent} keeps its questions when {orchestrator} starts it. If it does not, nobody approves each step.
html.meaning.orchestrator_vulnerable_ver: The flaw is public, so anyone who can reach {orchestrator} knows how to use it.
This copy is not running. It matters if {orchestrator} is started from it again.
html.meaning.orchestrator_network_listen: Anyone on the same network who reaches it can try to give work to your agents.
html.meaning.orchestrator_open_signup: With an account, they could give work to the agents {orchestrator} starts.
html.meaning.subagent_all_tools: A subagent meant for one task can then do everything {agent} can, including what that task never needed.
html.meaning.subagent_permissive_mode: When {agent} hands it a task, it acts without stopping to ask you.
html.meaning.subagent_permissive_mode.ye: When {agent} hands it a task, it does part of the work without asking you; how much depends on the mode.
html.meaning.subagent_hook_command: That command runs on your computer, with your permissions, when the subagent does what the hook watches.
html.meaning.subagent_inline_mcp: Those servers are not in the list you normally review, so they are easy to miss.
html.meaning.mcp_unpinned_launch: If that package is ever replaced by a malicious release, your agent would run it the next time it starts.
html.meaning.mcp_project_autoapprove: A project you did not write can then bring its own MCP servers, and Claude Code starts them without asking you about each one.
html.meaning.mcp_project_autoapprove.pro: In this project, Claude Code starts every MCP server the project brings without asking you about each one, also the ones added later.

html.headline.orchestrator_skips_approva: {orchestrator} can put {agent} to work without asking you.
html.headline.orchestrator_vulnerable_ve: Your {orchestrator} {version} has a known serious security flaw. It is fixed in {fixed}.
There is an {orchestrator} {version} in the npm cache with a known serious security flaw. It is fixed in {fixed}.
html.headline.orchestrator_network_liste: {orchestrator} listens beyond this computer: other devices can reach it.
html.headline.orchestrator_open_signup: Anyone who reaches {orchestrator} can create an account.
html.fix.orchestrator_network_listen: In {orchestrator}'s config.json, set it to listen only on this computer (bind: loopback).
html.headline.subagent_all_tools: The subagent {subagent} can use every tool {agent} has, because it doesn't list which ones.
html.headline.subagent_permissive_mode: The subagent {subagent} is set to work without asking you ({mode}).
html.headline.subagent_hook_command: The subagent {subagent} runs a command of its own when it acts.
html.headline.subagent_inline_mcp: The subagent {subagent} connects to MCP servers defined inside its own file.
html.subagent.user_folder: It is in your user folder, so it runs in every project without the folder-trust question.
html.fix.orchestrator_network_listen.pas: In {orchestrator}'s config.json, set daemon.listen back to 127.0.0.1:6767.
html.headline.mcp_unpinned_launch: {agent} starts the MCP server «{server}» with {launcher} and no fixed version: its code can change every time it starts.
html.fix.mcp_unpinned_launch: Pin an exact version, for example {package}@{example}.
html.headline.mcp_project_autoapprove: Claude Code approves every MCP server a project brings, on its own ({scope}).
html.fix.mcp_project_autoapprove: Remove enableAllProjectMcpServers and approve each server when Claude Code asks you.
